details:
AstroLogicX — Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

AstroLogicX is an interactive educational simulation that helps students understand the challenges of living and working on the Moon. In this project, the player takes the role of a mission commander responsible for a crew of four astronauts during a 10-day lunar mission.

The player must carefully manage four important resources: power, food, oxygen, and radiation protection. Through the mission dashboard, the commander can monitor resource levels, check astronaut health, track mission progress, and take actions such as charging solar power, producing food, generating oxygen, and activating radiation shielding. The simulation also includes unexpected events such as solar storms, moon dust storms, and equipment malfunctions. These events make the mission more challenging and encourage players to make thoughtful decisions. At the end, the system generates a mission report showing the results and the commander's performance.

The main benefit of AstroLogicX is that it makes space exploration concepts easier and more engaging to learn through interactive practice. Instead of only reading about astronaut challenges, students can experience simplified mission decisions and understand why resources, crew safety, and planning are important.

The intended impact is to encourage interest in space science and exploration while developing critical thinking, problem-solving, resource-management, and decision-making skills. It is designed especially for students and beginners who want to learn about lunar missions in an accessible way.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in Visual Studio Code. HTML was used to structure the application, CSS to create the space-themed interface and responsive layout, and JavaScript to implement the mission simulation, resource management, astronaut health tracking, random events, and mission report. The project is hosted online using Netlify.

The creative aspect of AstroLogicX is its combination of a space mission dashboard and a simple interactive learning game. It turns the responsibilities of a lunar mission commander into a hands-on experience. The Science Centre section also introduces basic concepts related to solar energy, hydroponic food production, oxygen generation, and radiation protection.

During development, important factors included making the project beginner-friendly, keeping the controls simple, creating a clear and engaging interface, balancing the resource-management challenges, including unexpected mission events, and ensuring that the website works on different screen sizes. The mission uses simulated values and rule-based events for educational purposes; it does not connect to live NASA systems or real-time NASA data.
